summary: 1846 is a lean, fast-playing 18xx that puts heavy pressure on route optimization and timing your train purchases before obsolescence wrecks a corporation; games run 2-4 hours rather than the 6+ of heavier 18xx titles. It's a cutthroat blend of stock manipulation and operational efficiency where dumping a corporation on other shareholders at the right moment is as important as good track building.
praised: Excellent introductory 18xx due to shorter length and cleaner rules
Tight, well-tuned economy with meaningful decisions every turn
Private company draft adds interesting asymmetric variety without a long auction
criticised: Still has significant downtime during other players' operating rounds
Multitasking as president of multiple corporations can be fiddly
Stock round dumping mechanics can feel mean and kingmaker-ish to newer players
Less depth/complexity than heavier 18xx titles for veteran fans

interaction.kind: stock manipulation, presidencies, and route competition

scoring.why: The winner is determined by total net worth (cash plus stock value plus private companies), driven by efficient train running and stock market timing
